1.he: יָפִיצוּ מֵעֲנַק שִׂכְלָם טוּרֵי לֶשֶׁם. וּמֵעֲנַן לִקְחָם נוֹזְלֵי גֶשֶׁם
1.note: A sound play: מֵעֲנַק "from the necklace" and מֵעֲנַן "from the cloud" differ by one letter. "Teaching" (לֶקַח) as rain recalls Deut 32:2.

2.note: Obscure. The verb is from Job 16:3 (מַה יַּמְרִיצְךָ). Read as "what does a ruler urge so strongly as generosity"; perhaps also "what spurs a ruler like generosity".

3.note: סָף is read from סוּף "to come to an end" (compare Ps 73:19 סָפוּ תַמּוּ). As a noun סַף is "threshold" or "basin", which gives no clear sense here.

4.note: The verb is from 1 Sam 2:33 (וְלַאֲדִיב אֶת נַפְשֶׁךָ, "to grieve your soul"). "Gentle" is a guess for the sense of the word here; the line can also be read "grief would have pained his heart".

5.he: וְעָלָיו אָמַר בְּחִיר ה': וְקֹבֵץ עַל-יָד יַרְבֶּה
5.note: "The chosen of the Lord" is Solomon, to whom Proverbs is ascribed. In Prov 13:11 עַל יָד means "little by little"; the old man takes it literally, the closed hand that gathers.

6.note: The same word twice: חֶסֶד "kindness" and חֶסֶד "disgrace" (Lev 20:17, Prov 14:34). The other pairs rhyme: יֹפִי/דֹּפִי, גְּדֻלָּה/נְבָלָה, אֱיָלוּת/שִׁפְלוּת, נְדָבָה/דִּבָּה (the last is נדבה without its first letter).

7.note: Literal. Elam (Persia) may be named for the rhyme with עוֹלָם and עֵילָם above; the point of the jibe is not clear.

8.he: וְכָל הַדָּבֵק בָּהּ כְּאִלּוּ דָבַק בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
8.note: An inversion of b. Ketubot 68a: whoever shuts his eyes to charity is as if he worshipped idols. The old man applies it to generosity itself.

9.note: Judg 4:11: Ḥeber the Kenite pitched his tent "as far as Elon-bezaanannim". The hero's name and dwelling come from that verse.

10.he: אֲנִי חֶבֶר וְכִשְׁמִי מַעֲשַׂי כִּי / אֲחַבֵּר נִפְזְרֵי מוּסָר בְּשִׁירִי
10.note: A pun: חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and אֲחַבֵּר "I join, I compose". The line break after כִּי is in the edition.
